newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower, seen rising on repo.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower, seen rising on repo.

text.p: Indian call money closed at 3.50-4.00 percent on Monday, down from the opening quote of 4.0-4.5 and unchanged from the weekend close, dealers said.
"Market was squarish, it opened higher at 4.5 percent, fell to 3.5 percent and closed up at 4.0 percent," a dealer said.
The RBI said it set a cut-off interest rate of 5.25 percent at a repo auction held on Monday.
The RBI said it received 16 bids for 6.20 billion rupees, of which it accepted 12 bids for 5.35 billion rupees.
"We expected RBI to mop up 10.0 billion rupees, while it could raise only 5.35 billion rupees," he said.
"The cut-off will restrict the call rates from opening below 5.50 percent on Tuesday", another dealer said.
But a dealer at a term-lending bank said call rates will continue at Monday's levels as most banks had covered their positions.
The prices of securities fell in thin trading day on Monday, dealers said. Interest shifted from the short -dated securities to longer-dated securities.
The 13.50 percent 1997 stock was traded at 102.45 rupees, lower compared to the previous price of 102.53 rupees, while 13.40 percent stock sliped by 15 basis points to 102.65 rupees.
Some dealers attributed the fall in prices to the forthcoming state loan auction scheduled for January 20 and the repo auctions by RBI.
In long-dated securities, the 13.85 percent 2006 rose by five basis point to 100.95 compared the Saturday's close.

The 364-day treasury bill maturing in December 1997 was traded at 10.30 percent yield compared to the previous close of 10.27 percent, while October 1997 maturity treasury bill was dealt at 10.25 percent against Saturday's yield of 10.21 percent, dealers said.
The 91-day treasury bills maturing in April 1997 was traded at 8.30 percent, higher compared to Saturday's yield of 8.21 percent, dealers said.
Commercial papers maturing in February 1997 were traded at 9.75 percent, dealers said.
